method: Tempo is read as the conventional four numbers written in seconds: lowering (eccentric), pause at the bottom, lifting (concentric) and pause at the top, so 3-1-2-0 means a three-second lower, a one-second pause, a two-second lift and no pause at the top. Seconds per rep is the sum of the four phases. Time under tension for a set is that per-rep time multiplied by the reps, and the block total multiplies the set time by the number of sets. Rests are counted between sets only, so rest total is the rest interval multiplied by one fewer than the number of sets, and block clock time is the tension total plus the rest total; a single set therefore carries no rest. The work-to-rest ratio compares one set's tension time with one rest interval and is reported as absent when rest is zero. Share under tension is the tension total divided by the block clock time. Every input is a whole number: each phase is 0-30 seconds with a lifting phase of at least 1 second, reps are 1-100, sets 1-50 and rest 0-1800 seconds, and anything else is refused with a specific message rather than parsed loosely. The tool is purely arithmetic on the user's own timing inputs: it does not assess whether a tempo, rep range or rest is suitable, does not estimate load, fatigue or muscle growth, and is not coaching or medical advice. It assumes every rep in a set uses the same tempo and that no time is spent on set-up or equipment changes. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: NSCA, Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning: repetition tempo is written as four phases — eccentric, bottom pause, concentric and top pause — in seconds.
ACSM, Resistance Training for Health and Fitness: time under tension is the duration a muscle is loaded during a set, the per-rep time multiplied by the reps.
Schoenfeld BJ, The mechanisms of muscle hypertrophy and their application to resistance training: rep duration and time under tension are treated as distinct training variables.
Baechle TR and Earle RW, Weight Training: Steps to Success: tempo notation such as 3-0-2-0 and rest intervals between sets are combined to plan a training block.
